name: Entity Graph
blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

nodes.scheme: DOI or arXiv id, linked to the original publisher
arXiv id from the model's own tags
registry id from the official MCP registry

reading.body:
The Entity Graph tracks 25,073 AI-related entities across companies, models, papers, regulations, and hardware, with open models vastly outnumbering proprietary API models by a factor of 36.

The dataset reveals structural asymmetry in AI infrastructure. Fifteen thousand open models exist against 428 tracked API models, yet the graph contains only 269 companies and 278 people. This suggests a fragmentation between the weight of available code and the concentration of commercial activity and decision-making power. The 1,788 papers cited by tracked models dwarf the 135 research papers directly monitored, indicating that model development relies on a deep tail of prior work rather than only flagship publications.

Regulatory and legal activity has become substantial. Four thousand three hundred and forty-three state AI bills and 109 lawsuits sit alongside 73 compliance documents standardized by ISO, NIST, and EU frameworks. This tracks a jurisdiction-specific and adversarial layer of AI development that varies by location. The graph does not quantify which bills are active, how lawsuits resolved, or which compliance standards apply to which companies, so it signals the existence of legal friction without measuring its impact.

The inclusion of 2,261 MCP servers and 37 hardware entries attempts to capture infrastructure below the model layer. This is sparse compared to the model and paper counts, and hardware entries are described as curated rather than exhaustive. The graph reflects what is catalogued and connected, not the full spectrum of physical systems driving AI compute, power, and buildings.
